nodes.summary: For every finite family $H$ of functions from a set $\alpha$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$ and all keys $x, y \in \alpha$, the number of functions $h \in H$ with $h(x) = h(y)$ is at most $|H|$.
nodes.title: Collision count is at most the family size

nodes.summary: For every finite family $H$ of functions from a set $\alpha$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$ and every key $x \in \alpha$, the collision count of $x$ with itself in $H$ equals $|H|$: $x$ collides with itself under every function in $H$.
nodes.title: A key collides with itself under the whole family

nodes.summary: For a finite family $H$ of functions from a set $\alpha$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$ and keys $x, y \in \alpha$, the collision count of $x$ and $y$ in $H$ is the number of functions $h \in H$ with $h(x) = h(y)$.
nodes.title: Collision count

nodes.summary: For every natural number $m$ and all distinct keys $x \ne y$ in a set $\alpha$, the collision count of $x$ and $y$ in the empty family of functions from $\alpha$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$, multiplied by $m$, is at most the size of the empty family, which is $0$.
nodes.title: The empty family satisfies the collision bound

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a finite set of indices from a type $\iota$, and let $h$ assign to each index $i \in \iota$ a function $h_i$ from a set $\alpha$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$. The family $h$ is universal on $s$ if $m > 0$, $s$ is nonempty, and for all distinct keys $x \ne y$ in $\alpha$ the number of indices $i \in s$ with $h_i(x) = h_i(y)$, multiplied by $m$, is at most $|s|$.
nodes.title: Indexed universal hash family

nodes.summary: A finite family $H$ of functions from a set $\alpha$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$ is universal if $m > 0$, $H$ is nonempty, and for all distinct keys $x \ne y$ in $\alpha$ the number of functions $h \in H$ with $h(x) = h(y)$, multiplied by $m$, is at most $|H|$; that is, $x$ and $y$ collide under at most a $1/m$ fraction of the members of $H$.
nodes.title: Universal hash family

nodes.summary: Let $p > 0$ and $m > 0$. A function $h$ from $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$ belongs to the mod-prime family of distinct functions exactly when $h = h_{a,b}$ for some index $(a, b)$ with $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $a \ne 0$, where $h_{a,b}$ is the mod-prime hash function with index $(a, b)$.
nodes.title: Members of the mod-prime family

nodes.summary:
Let $p$ be a prime and $m > 0$, and for $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with $a 
e 0$ let $h_{a,b}(x) = ((ax + b)  mod p)  mod m$ be the mod-prime hash function. For distinct keys $x 
e y$ in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, the number of index pairs $(a, b)$ with $a 
e 0$ and $h_{a,b}(x) = h_{a,b}(y)$, multiplied by $m$, is at most $p(p - 1)$, the total number of index pairs.
nodes.title: Collision bound for the mod-prime hash functions

nodes.summary: For $p > 0$ and $m > 0$, the mod-prime family is the finite set of all functions $h_{a,b}$ from $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$ with $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $a \ne 0$, where $h_{a,b}$ is the mod-prime hash function with index $(a, b)$.
nodes.title: Mod-prime family of distinct functions

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a natural number, $m > 0$ and $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, and write $\operatorname{val}(z)$ for the canonical natural-number representative of $z \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ (for $p = 0$, where $\mathbb{Z}/0\mathbb{Z} = \mathbb{Z}$, its absolute value), so that the mod-prime hash function is $h_{a,b}(x) = \operatorname{val}(ax + b) \bmod m$. For all keys $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, we have…
nodes.title: Collisions of a mod-prime hash function

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $p$ and $m$ with $m > 0$ and elements $a, b, x$ of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, the mod-prime hash value $h_{a,b}(x) \in \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$, read as a natural number, equals $\operatorname{val}(ax + b) \bmod m$. Here $ax + b$ is computed in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, and $\operatorname{val}(z)$ is the canonical natural-number representative of $z$: the residue in $\{0, \dots, p - 1\}$ when…
nodes.title: Value of the mod-prime hash

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $p$ and $m$ with $m > 0$ and elements $a, b$ of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, the mod-prime hash function $h_{a,b} \colon \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} \to \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$ is $h_{a,b}(x) = \operatorname{val}(ax + b) \bmod m$, where $ax + b$ is computed in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $\operatorname{val}(z)$ is the canonical natural-number representative of $z$ (the residue in $\{0, \dots, p - 1\}$…
nodes.title: Mod-prime hash function

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $p$ and $m$ with $m > 0$, the indexed mod-prime family assigns to each index $(a, b)$, with $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $a \neq 0$, the mod-prime hash function $h_{a,b} \colon \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} \to \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$.
nodes.title: Indexed mod-prime family

nodes.summary: For every positive natural number $p$, the set of pairs $(a, b)$ of elements of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with $a \neq 0$ has exactly $p(p - 1)$ elements.
nodes.title: Number of mod-prime indices

nodes.summary: For a natural number $p$, the index set of the mod-prime family is the set of pairs $(a, b)$ with $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $a \neq 0$.
nodes.title: Mod-prime index set

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $m$ a positive natural number. The indexed mod-prime family, whose member at the index $(a, b)$, with $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $a \neq 0$, is the mod-prime hash function $h_{a,b}$, is universal over the set of all such indices: this set is nonempty, and for all distinct keys $x \neq y$ in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, the number of indices $(a, b)$ with $h_{a,b}(x) = h_{a,b}(y)$,…
nodes.title: Universality of the mod-prime family

nodes.summary: For every type of keys $\alpha$ and every natural number $m$, the empty family of functions $\alpha \to \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$ is not universal: universality includes nonemptiness, since its meaning is a bound on the collision probability for a uniformly chosen member.
nodes.title: The empty hash family is not universal

nodes.summary: For every index type $\iota$, every type of keys $\alpha$, every natural number $m$ and every family $(h_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of functions $h_i \colon \alpha \to \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$, the family is not universal over the empty index set: indexed universality includes nonemptiness of the index set, since there is no uniform random choice from an empty family.
nodes.title: The empty indexed family is not universal

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $x \neq y$ be elements of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. For every index $(a, b)$ with $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $a \neq 0$, the image of $(a, b)$ under the pair bijection for $x, y$, viewed as an element of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, is the value of the pair map at $(a, b)$, namely $(ax + b, ay + b)$.
nodes.title: The pair bijection is given by the pair map

nodes.summary:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $x

nodes.title: Pair bijection of the CLRS counting argument

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a natural number, let $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, and let $(a, b)$ be an index of the mod-prime family, so that $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $a \ne 0$. Then the pair map at $x$ and $y$ sends $(a, b)$ to $(ax + b, ay + b)$.
nodes.title: Evaluating the pair map

nodes.summary:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $x 
e y$ be keys in the field $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. For every index $(a, b)$ of the mod-prime family, that is, $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with $a 
e 0$, we have $ax + b 
e ay + b$.
nodes.title: The two values of the pair map differ

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $x \ne y$ be keys in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. Then the pair map at $x$ and $y$, which sends an index $(a, b)$ of the mod-prime family (so $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $a \ne 0$) to $(ax + b, ay + b)$, is injective.
nodes.title: The pair map is injective

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a natural number and fix two keys $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. The pair map at $x$ and $y$ sends an index $(a, b)$ of the mod-prime family, that is, $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with $a \ne 0$, to the pair $(ax + b, ay + b) \in (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^2$ of inner hash values at $x$ and $y$.
nodes.title: The pair map of the mod-prime family

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
